title: Add declarative schema-backed collection listing
objective: Add a declarative schema-backed collection listing capability that maps each supported document schema and collection name to a constrained index expression, stable identifier selector, and human-readable text selector. Expose generic work-item and task list commands that show identifiers and textual descriptions in terminal output while preserving complete indexed objects in a versioned JSON response envelope.

branch.name: WI-0036-declarative-collection-listing
branch.rationale: The feature adds public collection-listing commands and a response contract, so implementation and review should be processed on a dedicated work-item branch before returning to the primary branch for release.

request.text: Create a new work item for declarative schema-backed collection listing. Define a registry that maps document schema and collection name to a constrained index expression, stable identifier selector, and human-readable text selector. Add generic work-item and task collection list commands. Human-readable output must show each item identifier and textual description; --json output must preserve the complete indexed objects in a versioned response envelope.

scope.name: declarative-collection-registry
scope.description: Define one versioned, schema-aware registry that maps a document schema and collection name to a constrained index expression, optional parent selection, stable identifier selector, and human-readable title/text selectors.
scope.reason: Collection-specific command implementations would duplicate path, identity, and display knowledge and would drift as the schema set grows.

scope.name: generic-document-indexing
scope.description: Implement a deterministic indexer that loads the existing JSON/YAML document representation, resolves exact constrained paths, supports nested parent collections, preserves document order, and returns the selected complete objects.
scope.reason: The collection commands need one safe selection mechanism instead of arbitrary JSONPath, executable expressions, or recursive document-wide ID searches.

scope.name: human-and-json-projections
scope.description: Render identifier plus declared textual description, with optional declared title, in human-readable mode and return complete indexed objects with source metadata in JSON mode.
scope.reason: Terminal output should be concise and useful while machine consumers must not lose fields from the selected document objects.

scope.name: work-item-and-task-cli
scope.description: Expose schema-aware collection list commands for work-item and task documents, including requirements, acceptance criteria, implementation objectives, and the other supported object-backed collections selected by the registry.
scope.reason: Users need a consistent command surface such as `sdlc work-item requirement list --work-item <id>` and `sdlc task objective list --task <id>`.

scope.name: versioned-response-and-validation
scope.description: Persist and validate a closed versioned response envelope for collection lists, test registry completeness and path failures, and preserve the existing single-reference resolution behavior.
scope.reason: The feature introduces a new output object and must provide durable contract and regression evidence without changing existing reference semantics.

nonGoals.name: arbitrary-jsonpath
nonGoals.description: Do not add arbitrary JSONPath, recursive descent, filter expressions, eval-based selectors, or user-supplied executable indexing expressions.
nonGoals.reason: The registry must remain deterministic, auditable, safe, and easy to validate.

nonGoals.name: invented-identifiers
nonGoals.description: Do not invent stable domain identifiers for collections whose schema items are plain strings or otherwise lack an authoritative identifier.
nonGoals.reason: Array positions are not equivalent to schema-owned entity identity; such collections may remain JSON-only or use explicitly documented positional display without entity references.

nonGoals.name: document-model-redesign
nonGoals.description: Do not redesign existing work-item or task payload schemas, rename existing fields, or duplicate task-specific collections into a common payload shape merely to support listing.
nonGoals.reason: The feature should index the current schema-backed documents declaratively rather than change their domain contracts.

nonGoals.name: reference-resolution-semantic-change
nonGoals.description: Do not change existing reference syntax, single-reference resolution semantics, global resource identity rules, or depth expansion behavior.
nonGoals.reason: Collection listing may reuse document loading and envelope infrastructure but must remain a separate collection projection capability.

nonGoals.name: remote-publication
nonGoals.description: Do not publish packages, deploy, or push branches or tags as part of implementation or validation; release remains a bounded local primary-branch operation.
nonGoals.reason: Local CLI and schema evidence does not establish external publication or deployment readiness.

items.name: declarative-collection-indexes
items.description: The collection-listing implementation must use a versioned declarative registry keyed by effective document schema and collection name, with constrained exact-path indexing and optional parent-item selection.
items.reason: A single declarative mapping is the reusable boundary for supporting many schema-defined arrays without one bespoke command implementation per collection.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Each supported collection definition declares its document schema selector, collection name, exact index path, and whether nested selection requires a parent identifier argument.

The indexer rejects unknown document-schema and collection combinations, missing paths, non-array paths, missing required parent selectors, and missing parent identifiers with structured findings rather than silently returning an unrelated value.
Indexing preserves source document order and does not use recursive document-wide identifier searches or arbitrary executable expressions.

items.name: declared-human-display
items.description: Every human-listable object-backed collection must declare how its item identifier and textual description are selected, with an optional title or name selector.
items.reason: The terminal view must consistently show meaningful identity and content without guessing between fields such as statement, description, question, summary, or name.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Human-readable list output shows each item’s authoritative unique identifier and declared textual description, and includes a declared title or name when the collection provides one.

A registry entry without a valid identifier or textual selector is rejected for human-list mode unless the collection is explicitly marked as lacking stable domain identity and excluded from entity-style listing.

Requirements, acceptance criteria, implementation objectives, research questions, findings, test cases, and representative task-specific collections display their schema-defined identifiers and textual fields without field-name-specific command code.

items.name: lossless-json-response
items.description: JSON mode must return a closed versioned collection response envelope containing source document metadata and the complete indexed objects without applying the human display projection.
items.reason: Automation and downstream consumers need every field from each selected object, not only the identifier and summary shown in terminal output.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A successful JSON response identifies its response schema, document schema, collection name, index expression, source document path and format, and returns every selected object unchanged under the collection data field.
An empty but valid collection returns a successful envelope with an empty data array, while selection and document failures return a valid envelope with structured findings and no fabricated items.
The collection response contract is persisted under schemas/, included in the schema audit, and has representative valid and invalid fixtures or equivalent instance-validation coverage.

items.name: schema-aware-cli-commands
items.description: The CLI must expose consistent schema-aware list commands for work-item and task collections while retaining the requested ergonomic command forms.
items.reason: Users should be able to list work-item requirements and task objectives through the same generic implementation boundary.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The CLI supports `sdlc work-item requirement list --work-item <work-item-id>` and `sdlc task objective list --task <task-id>` with human-readable identifier and text output.
The CLI supports `--json` for the collection commands and emits the complete versioned collection response envelope rather than the human display projection.

Nested collections such as work-item acceptance criteria require and honor an explicit parent selector, and task collection resolution selects definitions from the task’s declared task schema rather than from a hard-coded task-type branch table.
Unknown collection names, invalid identifiers, duplicate options, missing required selectors, and unresolved documents fail with actionable command errors and non-zero exit status.

items.name: compatibility-and-regression-evidence
items.description: The feature must be covered by focused indexer and CLI tests and must preserve existing reference-resolution behavior and repository-root boundaries.
items.reason: The implementation reuses document loading and response infrastructure that is already used by reference resolution, so regressions must be bounded explicitly.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Tests cover top-level and nested collections, schema-specific collection selection, identifier and text extraction, complete JSON object preservation, empty collections, invalid paths, duplicate identifiers, missing parents, and plain-string collections.
Existing single-reference resolution tests continue to pass with unchanged reference syntax, selected data semantics, global resource identity, and depth expansion behavior.
Typecheck, build, complete tests, schema audit, representative CLI list commands, and WI-0036 work-item validation pass before implementation is considered ready for review.

versionSuggestion.rationale: Adds schema-backed collection-listing commands and a versioned response envelope while preserving existing document and reference semantics.
versionSuggestion.disclaimer: This is an inferred recommendation; increase the impact if final changes introduce breaking command, schema, or reference behavior beyond the planned additive feature.
